title: Unify weight-format descriptor and decouple tokenizer adapter to simplify model load path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The model ingestion pipeline currently supports a variety of historical weight formats and shard conventions with ad-hoc heuristics sprinkled across the loader, manifest parser, and tokenizer-init code paths. This has led to several maintenance and performance problems: slow cold-starts when the tokenizers are initialized synchronously inside the weight activation loop, multiple places that try to infer shard layout causing mismatches, and regressions when quantized metadata is only available in some manifests. Goal: introduce a compact, versioned WeightFormatDescriptor header and a lightweight TokenizerAdapter handshake that together provide a single canonical surface for the loader to discover shard topology, dtype/quantization metadata, and tokenizer contract without special-casing legacy formats. We will implement a compatibility shim that can emit descriptors for legacy manifests so we can migrate incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: WeightFormatDescriptor spec approved in design doc and landed in repository
Unified loader can open all production manifests used in last 6 months (safetensors, legacy .ckpt shards, numpy shards) via descriptor or shim
TokenizerAdapter performs async handshake and no longer blocks model activation; cold-start latency reduced by >=20% on 1K token bootstrap benchmark
One rollout canary on dedicated staging fleet with automatic fallback to previous loader on error
No behavioral regressions in tokenization observed for the 10 canonical tokenizers in our regression suite
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Draft WeightFormatDescriptor spec (fields: version, shard_count, shard_order, dtype_map, quant_meta, preferred_mmap_hint). Publish design doc and gain eng/pm signoff.
Phase 2: Implement descriptor reader and compatibility shim that synthesizes descriptors for legacy manifests. Add unit tests covering synthesized descriptor correctness.
Phase 3: Implement TokenizerAdapter handshake that decouples tokenizer init from weight activation. Provide async callback and health probe for tokenizer readiness.
Phase 4: Integrate descriptor + tokenizer adapter into loader activation path behind feature flag. Add end-to-end benchmarks and memory profiles.
Phase 5: Canary rollout -> monitor metrics (cold-start latency, activation failures, memory usage) -> full rollout -> remove legacy heuristics and flags after 2 weeks of clean telemetry.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Descriptor spec misses an edge-case used by an older customer checkpoint. Mitigation: compatibility shim + exhaustive manifest fuzzing job and ops-runbook to roll back canary.
Risk: TokenizerAdapter introduces ordering bugs causing subtle decoding errors. Mitigation: add tokenization regression suite (10k prompts), deterministic golden checksums, and gated rollout.
Risk: Performance regressions when reading descriptor adds overhead. Mitigation: cache descriptors in blob metadata store and add mmap hint field for cold path optimization.
testing_plan: Unit tests for descriptor parsing and shim generation (CI)
Integration tests that spin up a small serve process and validate activation path with synthesized descriptors
Benchmark harness: 1K token cold-start benchmark across a representative set of 8 model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B) to measure tokenization and activation latencies
Canary metrics dashboard updates: activation_latency P50/P95, activation_failures, memory_peak, tokenizer_init_time
migration_steps: Create descriptor shims for existing manifests in model-registry (scripting job in infra) and store as <manifest>.descriptor.json
Enable feature flag in staging and run canary over a small % of production traffic
Run full validation pipeline comparing tokenization outputs for canary vs baseline for 72h
If stable, increase rollout percentage to 100% and schedule removal of legacy heuristics after two weeks
Follow-up: run a cleanup ticket to remove compatibility shim code and feature flags
